Beginning an independent native read-only final review of the entire PLAN2 P4.

Review scope covers P4.1-P4.23 and the AzGuard authorization phase. I will read mandatory inputs first, then inspect code and source documents.Beginning a systematic review of the authorization phase against normative requirements.

The review will return a JSON verdict with only confirmed defects. Code and phase verdicts may be split if runtime is clean but a gate blocks. A prior V1 composer test failed in TraceTest.php:13 due to an outdated trace-array assertion against the current Trace::record outcome. One replica was skipped in the ordinary suite, though a separate real replica run passed.

The stale TraceTest.php failure is not a security defect. V4 Pint and V5 PHPStan REDs are historical artifacts from preflight checks; expanded product-scoped runs passed. Three engines, Redis, replica/LSN, batch fence, and API checks all passed.

Type coverage is 99.32% and scratch controls passed. The V1 RED acceptance gate is the remaining blocker. It will likely force a phase_verdict of RED.

Inspecting TraceTest.php and Trace.php to determine the exact mismatch and owning item. The stale test will be judged against normative requirements from D14, D15, D16, the acceptance matrix, and dossier decisions before deciding if it blocks phase acceptance.The brief files are JSON, not markdown.Beginning a systematic review of critical security paths across the authorization phase.

Focusing on semantic boundaries most likely to contain defects. Verifying previously corrected slice findings. Strictly applying the rule that failures, skips, or unavailable results cannot be turned into GREEN. The V1 exact composer test RED is a trace assertion mismatch. The reviewer must establish actual owning items and acceptance consequences rather than assuming stale tests are security defects. GREEN requires no blockers or majors and honest acceptance; otherwise the verdict remains RED.

V1 is the exact `composer test` required acceptance gate in P4.14. Its RED verdict means the phase cannot be GREEN even if runtime is clean. The stale unit test assertion is a blocker/major.

The review will likely produce a split verdict. Code_verdict may be GREEN if no security or semantic defects are found. Phase_verdict will remain RED because the required V1 composer test acceptance is still failing. The stale unit test failure is being evaluated as a potential blocker.

The stale test is a product defect of the test suite. It expects an outdated Trace::record contract that predates intentional signature changes in P4.1 and P4.10. The test asserts old keys like 'result' while the code now produces 'outcome', 'detail', and other updated fields. This mismatch directly causes the V1 composer test failure.

The stale test is a test defect, not a security finding. It fails the V1 composer test acceptance gate because the Trace shape evolved with extra keys and reordered fields. The underlying behavior remains correct: silent steps are still stored only when requested.

The stale test failure is a confirmed defect, not cosmetic. It is a major issue because it directly causes the required V1 composer test to fail.

The stale test was added in this phase diff alongside the new implementation. It was never updated after Trace::record gained outcome and detail fields. The owner is P4.10 explain, since those extra fields are explain-related.Beginning a deep review of the critical security code.

Focusing on P4.8 through P4.23 cache and freshness logic. Verifying cache key composition, expiration, and tenant partitioning. Checking Primary versus Default replica freshness, unsupported host transaction handling, lock-first joint root and mutate marker ordering, and guard leave code-only policy enforcement.

Expanding the review to cover retry fences, scalar semantics, pagination visibility, D44 budgets, Redis, V43 latency, replica LSN, API manifest, regression specs, CRM README, and residuals.

A potential issue was spotted: isSuperAdmin returns false after three ReadAttemptChanged retries instead of throwing ConsistencyError. D15 treats this as diagnostic rather than an authorization decision.

Reconsidered the isSuperAdmin inconsistency path. Fail-closed behavior for a diagnostic query may be acceptable. This likely does not constitute a defect.

PermissionSetCache::get correctly filters expired items at read time from memory using activeAt($now).

Cache put stores Grant and RoleContribution objects serialized by Laravel cache.

Verifying that cached Grant objects contain only raw authority data and no final Allow decisions. The cache key includes generation, subject, tenant, contexts, source, readMode, and authority. D25 specifies codec as implicit in the digest function, but the Russian key description explicitly lists codec.

The cache key is built by IdentityCodec::digest over revision, generation, subject, tenant, contexts, source, readMode, and authority. Codec version may be implicit inside that digest rather than explicitly listed in the key string.

Tenant-partition cache revision promotion must ensure one tenant's state change invalidates only that tenant's cache while leaving other tenants untouched.

rememberState clears all sets when a key's state changes. The tenant partitioning mechanism needs inspection.

forgetState invalidates every tenant globally rather than isolating to one. This is overly broad but fail-closed and not a security defect.

A potential bug was spotted in get(): Redis unserialization might return a string instead of DateTimeImmutable for validUntil, causing the expiration check to fail and return null. This would be fail-closed behavior, so Redis serialization tests are needed.

get() only clears expired entries from memory when validUntil is past. It does not delete the stale Redis key, so an expired entry may linger until its TTL expires. Clock skew could allow a later read to re-fetch that expired value before Redis evicts it.

The Redis expiration bug is not a security issue. The memory check rejects expired entries before they are used.

Need to verify that ReadAttempt and AuthorityStage do not skip policy, restriction, or condition checks based on cached grants or role contributions.Beginning the read-only review by carefully examining the critical sections of the source files.Beginning the review by examining the fence protocol.

D15 limits each fenced source to three attempts. DatabaseSource::fenced() already retries up to three times. ReadAttempt adds another whole-attempt fence. Authorizer retries on ReadAttemptChanged up to three times. These overlapping retry loops risk exceeding the three-attempt cap.

Checking whether ReadAttempt.databaseItems uses the pinned session's readAssignments or DatabaseSource::fenced(). If it calls the latter, the inner retry loop would nest after dynamic prepare was already accepted. That would violate the single whole fence rule.I am beginning a careful review to identify real defects.

Visibility.php line 152 blocks NotGrantable role contributions without exception for automatic FolderSource roles. AuthorityStage already allows this case.

This creates a fail-closed visibility gap. A user who can scalar-decide Allow may be hidden from visibleTo. That violates exact visibility parity (P14) and D66.

I am pausing to verify whether automatic NotGrantable roles are actually a real path. The Dossier and RootRole examples suggest they may be valid. I must confirm this before labeling the visibility.php discrepancy as a confirmed defect.

The superadmin role is a concrete example of an automatic NotGrantable role. Visibility.php line 152 would skip the superadmin witness entirely, while scalar decide still allows it. This confirms a significant exact visibility parity bug. I am now checking whether the Dossier example marks superadmin as grantable.

The Dossier example confirms RootRole is both #[NotGrantable] and #[GrantedAutomatically]. This validates the exact visibility parity bug. Scalar decide allows automatic NotGrantable roles, but Visibility.php drops them entirely. The former keys path is correct.

The bug is owned by P4.12 visibility integration. D15 §2 and §5 specify that automatic FolderSource roles can bypass grantable=false, but Visibility.php lacks both the source-type check and the GrantedAutomatically trait check.

The defect is confirmed as a code bug. Severity is major because it under-includes authorized rows and violates exact visibility parity, which is an acceptance requirement. I will now inspect TenantAdminRole, SuperAdmin tests, and WitnessBranchesTest to verify whether CRM superadmin roles are grantable.

I am now comparing membership and restriction application across the Visibility.php branches. The Grants path applies conditions and role eligibility before permission matching, while scalar MembershipRestriction is applied once after qualification. I am also verifying whether the PolicyOnly path correctly scopes common eligibility to the group level.

The Grants path applies conditions and role eligibility before the permission-matching continue. Non-matching branches are discarded after constraint, so this ordering is correct.

I am now questioning whether the Visibility.php comment about role eligibility is accurate. The code only applies conditions and mapping scope constraints, not explicit ScopeEligibility checks per contribution.

I also noted that D15 §3 explicitly forbids automatic roles without an exact adapter, yet FolderSource visibility selections rely on contextsCovering.

I am now examining the Gate's dynamicLocal behavior. When a permission is unknown and the catalog is dynamic, the gate catches UnknownPermissionException and returns null if dynamicLocal is true.

D26 and D65 reveal a security defect in the Gate's dynamicLocal handling. When a dot-separated ability is missing from both static and dynamic catalogs, the gate returns null instead of deny. D65 requires qualified unknown owned keys to be refused. Returning null allows Laravel to fall through to other policies and potentially grant access. This is a concrete security gap.

I am now reading PanelResolver::owner and Gate tests to confirm whether dotted abilities are misclassified as owned when the dynamic catalog is active.

I also found a stale assertion in TraceTest.php. The test was written for the old Trace::record signature and still expects the old shape. Because P4.10 likely extended record() with outcome and detail, the owner of this broken test is P4.10.

I am now weighing whether the stale TraceTest is a blocker or minor issue. The user explicitly states that required acceptance is still RED, so the phase verdict must reflect this. I will check phase patches and comments to confirm which item changed the Trace::record signature.

The review instructions explicitly require a RED phase verdict if any required acceptance remains RED. A minor test failure therefore blocks phase approval. The stale TraceTest assertion is a confirmed blocker.

The stale TraceTest is a real acceptance failure, not a cosmetic issue. A single failing test in composer test makes the phase verdict RED. Severity is minor because the underlying trace behavior still holds.

I will inspect V1.log to confirm the exact failure message and verify that only one test failed. The original validation defects V4 and V5 are historical artifacts, not current product blockers, because the expanded checks now pass.

V4 and V5 are historical validation artifacts. V4 is a preflight artifact outside the product. V5 is an unused ContextAware trait with no configured source caller. Both original defects remain classified separately from runtime. The expanded checks pass.

I will inspect V4.log and V5.log to confirm the original validation failures are historical artifacts. I am also checking whether existing SuperAdmin or WitnessBranches tests already cover the automatic NotGrantable role path, which would determine if that visibility gap is already tested.Confirmed the V1 failure stems from key ordering and extra outcome/detail fields.

The failure is a stale exact-array assertion. Pest's `->and()` chain likely masked the silent path, but the diff confirms extra keys in the actual array.FolderSource::contextsCovering returns null when any automatic role exists.

ReadAttempt::selections throws VisibilityNotSupportedException on null. Automatic roles therefore trigger an unsupported exception rather than silent skipping. The grantable check in Visibility.php only applies to returned contributions, so NotGrantable automatic roles are not silently dropped; the entire visibleTo call fails.

This fail-closed behavior is documented. It may be overly strict for automatic superadmin roles, but it aligns with the unsupported rule for arbitrary automatic roles without exact adapters. The grantable skip correctly applies to stored NotGrantable and grantable roles. Automatic roles never reach that line because selection returns null first. This only holds when roleClasses is empty and discovery contains no automatic roles.

The suspected visibility bug is not a silent allow/deny mismatch. It throws unsupported. Need to confirm ReadAttempt throws before partial results.

ReadAttempt throws VisibilityNotSupportedException before query execution. Custom non-FolderSource contributions cannot bypass NotGrantable checks, so both visibility and scalar paths yield zero authority for them.

D15 parity tests require fail-closed outcomes and missing rows for unsupported exact components, not returned sets. Throwing unsupported is therefore correct rather than a defect.

Gate dynamic null is intentional and tested. Tests at lines 82-91 expect foreign.dynamic to abstain when the catalog is dynamic. Returning null for unknown dotted names is correct behavior. PanelResolver comments confirm that dynamic catalogs return tentative candidates for adapter confirmation. GateBridge logic handles this same case.

Prefixed panels return the panel directly without catalog checks. UnknownPermissionException is caught and rethrown as a deny response. Tests expect admin.orders.unknown to be denied.

D26 requires unknown owned actions to be denied. This conflicts with the documented abstain behavior for missing dynamic names. The tension between these two rules needs resolution.

The abstain behavior for unconfirmed dynamic names is a deliberate implementation choice. It prevents foreign dotted names on dynamic panels from being stolen. This may conflict with D26's explicit requirement to deny unknown owned actions, but the design comment treats dynamic membership as tentative until adapter confirmation.

The abstain behavior for unconfirmed dynamic names is explicitly encoded in P4.11 acceptance text and resolver comments, so it should not be reported as a defect.

D26 permits early host Gate.before to run before the adapter, which aligns with Laravel's before callback execution order.

Re-examining the user requirement "early host before cannot override ours" suggests it may mean an early Gate::before returning null or false should not override AzGuard's own decision once AzGuard owns the ability. The exact scope of this prohibition is being reconsidered.

D26 confirms that early host Gate::before may run before the adapter. The requirement "early host before cannot override ours" means that once AzGuard produces a decision, a later host after/before hook cannot turn a deny into an allow. Laravel's Gate::before short-circuits on non-null responses, which is a known limitation.The user noted that an early host cannot override the current setup.

The P4.11 contract and 09 §7 explicitly permit early host Gate::before to bypass the bridge as a documented integration limitation. The user's instruction likely targets AzGuard's own before hooks rather than host hooks, since BeforeResult only supports Deny or Continue. Coverage item 5 requires authoritative Gate authority for ours and null for foreign, with early host before excluded from overriding.

Early host Gate::before is a documented integration limitation in P8.2, not a P4 defect. Reporting it as a defect would contradict the no-future-write-API-gaps rule and the explicit residual. It should be excluded from P4 findings.

The user's checklist item is a compressed and imprecise restatement of the normative requirement. The adopted dossier documents the limitation rather than demanding its removal. Laravel's before hook chain runs sequentially until a non-null result halts execution, so a bridge hook registered first naturally prevents later host hooks from overriding it.

The host-before override is confirmed as an accepted P8.2 residual and will not be reported as a defect.

A retry counting bug was found. The outer evaluate() loop and the inner group retry logic both increment attempt counters. Nested retries can exceed the D15 limit of three whole attempts before a ConsistencyError is thrown.

The outer attempt loop only retries when prepare() throws ReadAttemptChanged or DecisionSet throws ConsistencyException. group() catches ReadAttemptChanged internally and returns ConsistencyError decisions on the final retry instead of rethrowing. DecisionSet throws on conflicting state tokens for the same storage or panel. If setAttempt is below two, the entire set retries; at attempt two, conflicting decisions become ConsistencyError. This yields up to nine database fences in the worst case, exceeding the spec's three-attempt limit. Extra retries are conservative and fail-closed, but they violate the explicit maximum and should be reported as a confirmed defect.

The outer attempt loop is unbounded. It uses `for ($setAttempt = 0; ; $setAttempt++)` with no upper bound, and the `continue` on `ReadAttemptChanged` never checks a limit. `prepare()` throws that exception whenever `terminal` is false, which is true for every attempt before the third. This means the loop can retry indefinitely, not merely up to three times.

The outer attempt loop is actually bounded. After the third attempt, prepare() stops throwing ReadAttemptChanged, so the loop cannot retry indefinitely. DecisionSet also halts at attempt two and returns, preventing unbounded retries.
